bull_bear.body: - Conservative — no large capex committed; cash deployed into pet-food brand build (imports + marketing first, plant later) and the Ecuador investment. (Dividend policy not discussed on this call.)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **RM inflation (acute):** fish-meal/soya spike could compress H1 FY27 feed margins before hikes fully pass through; further escalation if El Niño hits the kharif crop.
- **Fish-meal export drain:** ~75% of India-made fish meal is exported (price + GoI incentives; 5% GST on local purchase vs nil on exports) — Avanti + FMA + CLFMA lobbying GoI to curb fish-meal exports/incentives and to allow soya-meal imports (done once before, ~2003). Policy outcome uncertain.
- **US tariff structure unresolved:** post-IEEPA, US introduced a temporary Section-122 (Trade Act 1974) global surcharge from 24-Feb-2026 for up to 150 days, initially 10% but "indications of a possible increase" — final seafood tariff still unclear.
- **Refund timing/quantum risk:** USD 15-20m still being validated; AD/CVD review suspension means 12-18-month wait.
- **Demand/biological risk:** shrimp culture depends on disease, climate, farm-gate prices; Q2 still ahead.
- **Budgeting blackout:** management cannot yet frame an FY27 budget — low forward visibility.
- **Ecuador competition** remains #1 exporter (though Ecuador "issues" emerging may help India).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Candid and operationally detailed; JMD repeatedly deferred technical questions to the right divisional ED/CFO (good bench). Honest about not being able to budget FY27 and about margin pressure; measured (not promotional) on export-growth pace, explicitly rejecting "exponential" growth in favour of step-by-step quality-gated scaling. Some answers vague on capacity ("send an email"). Realistic on pet food being a long brand-build.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The IEEPA refund (~USD 15-20m) is a real, quantified but back-ended optionality — a future other-income/PBT kicker not in current numbers, gated by AD/CVD review timing (12-18 months). Track ACE filings and the suspension-of-liquidation lift.
- Feed (the cash cow) is entering a margin air-pocket: spot fish meal (INR 230-240) is already ~INR 100 above the Q4 consumption average (INR 130), so reported feed margins likely worsen further in Q1 FY27 until the next price hike lands — a near-term negative the strong FY26 PBT masks.
- Mix is quietly de-risking from the US: US volume fell -17.9% while China/EU/Japan grew sharply; the export division (not feed) drove FY26 profit growth (+107% PBT) — Avanti is becoming less a pure feed play and more a balanced feed + value-added-export + (nascent) pet-food group.
- The fish-meal export issue is a domestic policy lever: if GoI curbs fish-meal exports/incentives, it directly relieves Avanti's single biggest input — a regulatory catalyst worth tracking.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet FY26: Reserves and Surplus Rs 36,944 mn on Share capital of Rs 136 mn; Total Equity and Liabilities Rs 42,604 mn (FY25: Rs 31,612 mn, Rs 136 mn and Rs 36,827 mn).
- Key ratios FY26 versus FY25: RoCE 22.30% vs 23.00%, RoE 19.09% vs 19.00%, Net debt to equity 0.01x in both years, Interest coverage 320x vs 329x.
- Non-current assets rose from Rs 9,187 mn (FY25) to Rs 14,275 mn (FY26) while current assets moved from Rs 27,640 mn to Rs 28,329 mn; the deck gives no capex figure, project list or explanation for the non-current-asset step-up.
- No dividend, buyback or capital-allocation policy statement appears anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Shrimp Feed (Avanti Feeds standalone):** FY26 gross income INR 4,538 cr (-0.2% YoY, lower Apr-25 prices), PBT INR 715 cr (+8.66%); FY volume 5,62,060 MT (vs 5,55,248). Major RMs: fish meal, soya-bean meal, wheat flour (+ fish oil, soya lecithin, soya oil). Avg consumption cost Q4: fish meal INR 130/kg (Q3 117, Q4FY25 91); soya meal INR 55 (Q3 44, Q4FY25 41); wheat flour INR 31 (down). **Current purchase prices: fish meal INR 230/kg, soya meal INR 72/kg, wheat flour INR 30/kg** — i.e. spot fish meal already INR 100 above Q4 avg.
- **Processing & Export (Avanti Frozen Foods):** FY26 gross income INR 1,741 cr (+43% YoY), PBT INR 178 cr (+107%); volume 16,976 MT (+2,827, +20%). Avanti is **importer-of-record in the US** (does its own customs clearance + delivery). Stated effective/installed capacity ~26,000-28,000 MT but seasonally constrained on raw-material availability. Heavy value-add mix (ready-to-eat/cooked, breading, shrimp drinks, Japanese preparations) — among India's larger value-added producers; food-ingredients partnership; R&D being accelerated.
- **Pet Food (Avanti Pet Care, "Avant Furst"):** cat + dog food, currently imported from Thailand to Avanti formulations (own plant pending). Q4 sales INR 151 lakh. On Amazon + Supertails; digital marketing (Instagram/Facebook). Tier-1 led, entering Tier-2/3.
- **Ecuador:** Avanti has invested into Ecuador shrimp in partnership with a union/co-op — a global-supply-chain hedge alongside India.

latest_quarter.body:
- **Feed margin squeeze is the headline risk:** fish meal doubled INR 100→240/kg in two months (May-Jun), soya meal +~45%, driven by Gulf War (supply) + El Niño (crop failure fear). Soya tightness from 13-lakh-ton prior-year crop shortfall; GoI raised soya MSP ~INR 380/quintal (to INR 5,708). Mitigation = feed price hikes (one taken Feb-26, only ~1 month partial impact in Q4; another imminent) — management "confident cost will be absorbed to a great extent" but not fully.
- **Export margin:** structurally above market on value-add mix; FY26 helped by FX, lower ocean freight, higher realizations. Trade-off: more value-add → lower factory output.
- **Labour-code provisions** (gratuity + leave encashment) dented both divisions' Q4 PBT.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Consol gross income INR 1,515 cr (+5.86% YoY), PBT INR 184 cr (-12.8% YoY) on feed RM squeeze + labour-code provision; FY26 consol PBT INR 882 cr (+20%). Export div the FY star (PBT +107% to INR 178 cr on +20% volume/FX). Spot fish meal doubled to INR 230-240/kg, soya +45% (Gulf War + El Niño) → feed price hike imminent. IEEPA tariffs invalidated; ~USD 15-20m refund expected (12-18 mo, AD/CVD-gated); US account opened. Pet food at ~100 MT (target 800). No big capex 2 yrs. FY27 guide: feed ~5.8 lakh MT, exports ~19,000 MT, group growth ~10-15%; mgmt can't yet budget FY27.
- _Next Q → check: (1) magnitude/timing of the new feed price hike vs fish-meal at INR 230+; (2) Q1 feed margin (peak-season volume vs RM spike); (3) any IEEPA refund actually received + Section-122 final tariff; (4) soya-meal import permission outcome + GoI fish-meal export curbs; (5) pet-food run-rate toward 800 MT + plant DPR/approval; (6) US vs China/EU export mix; (7) Ecuador contribution._

outlook.body:
- **Feed volume:** FY27 feed sales ~5,80,000 MT (vs 5,62,060 MT FY26, ~+3%). Industry shrimp production CY26 est. 8-9 lakh MT → total feed consumption 11-12 lakh MT.
- **Export volume:** FY27 frozen-shrimp exports ~19,000 MT (vs 16,976 MT FY26, ~+12%); management defended this as deliberately step-by-step (quality/food-safety constrained), not aggressive despite EU-FTA access.
- **Feed price hikes:** another feed price increase coming "in the next few days / one week-10 days" to absorb the RM spike; quantum being finalized against market acceptability.
- **Pet food:** scaling 53 → 100 MT now, target ~800 MT by year-end; 31 distributors / 13 cities; new SKUs (treats, economy food, wet food) coming.
- **Capex:** "no big capex in the next two years" for feed or processing (growth via utilization, not capacity). Pet-food Hyderabad plant land converted, designs being finalized — construction only after DPR + govt approvals.
- **Overall:** group revenue + profit growth targeted ~10-15% over 2-3 yrs ("a big achievement" given uncertainty); management explicitly says it cannot yet prepare an FY27 budget.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Not an order-book business. Visibility = farmer stocking cycle: Q1 (Apr-May-Jun) is peak shrimp-culture season and is "progressing without much hurdles"; Q2 (Jul-Sep) equally important to complete season 1. Farm-gate shrimp prices stable, export market described as "promising / looking bright" (US + EU).
- Pipeline-equivalent catalysts: EU FTA (better market access, build slowly); possible US bilateral trade deal; IEEPA tariff-refund processing.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **IEEPA tariff refund (key optionality):** US Supreme Court 20-Feb-2026 (6-3) ruled IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs; reciprocal tariffs invalidated; CBP stopped collecting IEEPA tariffs from 24-Feb-2026. Avanti Frozen (importer-of-record) will file ACE-portal entries; estimated refund ~USD 15-20m; US bank account already opened (a refund pre-condition). Caveat: Indian frozen-shrimp entries since 1-Apr-2025 are suspended pending AD/CVD administrative reviews → refunds expected only as suspension lifts, ~12-18 months.
- **EU FTA:** improved access; multi-year volume build (quality/safety gated).
- **Value-added shrimp:** structurally higher margin than peers; deliberate balance vs commodity throughput (more value-add = lower physical output).
- **Pet food:** early but management is bullish ("expecting a lot of growth").
- **Geographic diversification:** China +24%, EU +36%, Japan +5% in FY26 (vs US -17.9% by volume) — reducing single-geography dependence.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Consolidated FY26 was a strong year driven mainly by the Frozen/Export division, refunds 12-18 months out) plus improving US/EU shrimp demand, but management is openly unable to even budget FY27 given the uncertainty.
